answer: Sybil resistance via timber-staked vouching with echo detection: new agent identities must lock timber, verifiable compute-time tokens taking hours to generate, making mass identity creation expensive. Each identity accrues a relic, a non-transferable record of honest epoch participation. When agents transact, an echo of relic history propagates to counterparties; sybil clusters reveal as echo chambers with dense internal vouches but no external relic lineage. An attacker creating 1000 fakes pays 1000x timber cost plus weeks of relic aging for isolated influence only.
